#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dispatch a child workflow and wait for it — NEVER kill it (gh-1903).
# Shared by every dispatching daily-publish leg.
#
# gh-1903 invariant: a child run QUEUED behind siblings on the single
# self-hosted runner (fa-m5-1) is NORMAL OPERATION, not a failure mode.
# The 2026-10-26 incident (daily run 40274465122, issue #1735) cancelled
# TWO healthy queued testflight children (~31m "queue stall" each) and
# failed a fully-built v1.0.648 release solely by killing its place in
# line. What remains here:
#   * dispatch + exact run correlation, unchanged (#343 below);
#   * a read-only wait: child state + elapsed logged every poll, sibling
#     in-progress runs logged on a diagnostic interval while the child has
#     not started — NO stall timer, NO wedge cancel, NO re-dispatch;
#   * bounds: the child's own per-job server-side timeouts (#344) and the
#     leg's timeout-minutes — nothing else;
#   * exactly ONE cancel path: when the LEG itself is terminated (leg
#     timeout, manual cancel → this script gets TERM/INT), cancel only
#     THIS leg's own NEVER-STARTED child (by the already-correlated run
#     id) so an orphaned queued run cannot publish unattended when the
#     pool revives, then fail with a diagnostic naming the child run, its
#     last observed state, and the observed pool activity. A child that
#     ever started, or already completed, is never touched.
#
# The watchdog it replaces (kept for history): #344 budgeted the watch
# (~2x historical duration) and cancelled + re-dispatched a wedged run
# once; gh-172 added a queue-stall window (no in_progress job for
# max(600, budget/8)s) for the pool-held zombie (run 39374894901). Both
# heuristics false-positive on healthy queues by construction — 31m does
# not cover the cli sibling chain's 335m worst-case on the same runner —
# and each cancel loses the queue position and restarts the clock, a
# starvation loop. Zombie handling is now: CANNOT OBSERVE ⇒ CANNOT JUDGE.
# The repo-wide `gh run list --status in_progress` probe is read-only; if
# it shows runs, the queue is presumed healthy; if it shows none while the
# child never started, a ::warning:: names the gh-172 zombie signature and
# the leg timeout surfaces the full diagnostic. Only a repo-wide EMPTY
# in_progress list while the child never started positively establishes
# pool idleness — and even then the script does not cancel (gh-1903).
#
# #343 — correlation (unchanged): the TestFlight and Play legs dispatch
# the SAME workflow (build-mobile.yml) as concurrent `needs: plan`
# siblings; identifying "our" run by event + a createdAt window only let
# the Play leg latch the TestFlight run. Correlation here:
#   * exact displayTitle match (--title) — the child workflow's run-name
#     embeds its inputs, so the sibling's differently-shaped run can never
#     be adopted (`gh run list` cannot filter by inputs; displayTitle is
#     the only distinguisher in the list API);
#   * the NEWEST matching run ([-1]) — never [0];
#   * a tight 30s createdAt window (clock-skew headroom; a run from
#     minutes ago is out of scope).
#
# Usage:
#   dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO --ref main \
#     [--title 'run-name exact match'] [--out-run-id FILE] [-f key=value]...
#
# The run id is written to --out-run-id as soon as correlation succeeds
# (BEFORE the wait), so callers can export the run URL even when the
# child run later fails. Env knobs (test shims): DW_POLL_SECONDS (60),
# DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS (10), DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS (60),
# DW_DIAG_SECONDS (300 — sibling-liveness probe interval while the child
# has not started; 0 = every poll).
set -euo pipefail

workflow=""
repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-}"
ref="main"
title=""
out_run_id=""
inputs=()

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --repo) repo="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --ref) ref="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --title) title="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --out-run-id) out_run_id="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    -f) inputs+=( -f "$2" ); shift 2 ;;
    -*) echo "dispatch_and_watch: unknown flag: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    *)
      if [ -n "$workflow" ]; then
        echo "dispatch_and_watch: unexpected extra arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
      fi
      workflow="$1"; shift
      ;;
  esac
done
if [ -z "$workflow" ] || [ -z "$repo" ]; then
  echo "usage: dispatch_and_watch.sh WORKFLOW.yml --repo OWNER/REPO [--ref main] [--title T] [--out-run-id FILE] [-f k=v]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

poll="${DW_POLL_SECONDS:-60}"
appear_poll="${DW_APPEAR_POLL_SECONDS:-10}"
appear_attempts="${DW_APPEAR_ATTEMPTS:-60}"
diag="${DW_DIAG_SECONDS:-300}"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

# ── gh-1903 single cancel path: the orphan-cleanup trap ────────────────────
# Leg timeout / manual cancel make the runner TERM (then KILL) this
# script. On TERM/INT: if OUR child was never started and is not completed,
# cancel exactly that run (gh-172 containment — an orphaned queued run
# must not publish unattended when the pool revives) and fail naming the
# child, its last observed state, and the observed pool activity. A child
# that ever started — even if it is between jobs right now — is left
# alone: its own per-job server-side timeouts (#344) bound it.
run_id=0
child_started=0
watch_started=0
last_state="(never polled)"
pool_note="no pool observation yet"

orphan_cleanup() {
  local sig="$1" ec=143 now
  [ "$sig" = "INT" ] && ec=130
  now=$(date +%s)
  if [ "$run_id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null \
      && [ "$child_started" -eq 0 ] \
      && [ "${last_state%%/*}" != "completed" ]; then
    echo "::error::leg terminated by $sig after $((now - watch_started))s — child $workflow run $run_id NEVER STARTED (last observed: $last_state; $pool_note); cancelling this orphaned child only (gh-1903 orphan-cancel) — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
    gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
      || echo "::warning::orphan cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)" >&2
  else
    echo "::error::leg terminated by $sig after $((now - watch_started))s — child $workflow run $run_id (started: $([ "$child_started" -eq 1 ] && echo yes || echo no); last observed: $last_state; $pool_note); nothing to cancel (gh-1903: never-started children only)" >&2
  fi
  exit "$ec"
}
trap 'orphan_cleanup TERM' TERM
trap 'orphan_cleanup INT' INT

dispatch
epoch=$(date +%s)
if ! run_id=$(wait_for_run "$((epoch - 30))"); then
  echo "::error::dispatched $workflow run never appeared (no workflow_dispatch run${title:+ titled \"$title\"} in the trailing window after $((appear_attempts * appear_poll))s)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "watching $workflow run $run_id${title:+ (\"$title\")} — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id — read-only wait, no stall timer, no re-dispatch (gh-1903)"
if [ -n "$out_run_id" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$run_id" > "$out_run_id"; fi

watch_started=$(date +%s)
last_diag=0
while :; do
  # One poll = one API call (gh-172 review): status, conclusion and the
  # running-job count arrive atomically — no race where two calls
  # straddle a completion. A failed poll cannot observe, so it cannot
  # judge (gh-172): it is logged and the wait simply continues — the
  # bounds are the child's per-job server-side timeouts (#344) and the
  # leg timeout, and there is no heuristic left to poison.
  observed="$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion,jobs \
    --jq '"\(.status)/" + (.conclusion // "-") + " " + ([.jobs[] | select(.status == "in_progress")] | length | tostring)' 2>/dev/null)" || observed=""
  if [ -z "$observed" ] || [ "${observed%% *}" = "$observed" ]; then
    status="error/-"
    running=""
    last_state="$status"
    echo "poll failed (gh/API unreachable) after $(( $(date +%s) - watch_started ))s — cannot observe, cannot judge (gh-172); the wait continues"
  else
    status="${observed%% *}"
    running="${observed##* }"
    last_state="$status"
    if [ -n "$running" ] && [ "$running" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
      child_started=1
    fi
    echo "child $run_id: $status running_jobs=${running:-unknown} elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - watch_started ))s (started: $([ "$child_started" -eq 1 ] && echo yes || echo 'not yet — queued is healthy, gh-1903'))"
  fi
  if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
  now=$(date +%s)

  # gh-1903 read-only zombie diagnostics: while the child has not started,
  # probe repo-wide liveness on the diagnostic interval. This NEVER
  # cancels — it only distinguishes "queued behind siblings" (healthy)
  # from "pool appears idle but the child never starts" (the gh-172
  # zombie signature, surfaced in full at the leg timeout above).
  if [ "$child_started" -eq 0 ] && [ $((now - last_diag)) -ge "$diag" ]; then
    last_diag="$now"
    if sibs="$(gh run list --repo "$repo" --status in_progress --limit 20 \
        --json databaseId,displayTitle \
        --jq '[.[] | select(.databaseId != '"$run_id"')] | length as $n | "\($n) in_progress run(s): " + ([.[] | "\(.databaseId) \(.displayTitle)"] | join("; "))' 2>/dev/null)"; then
      if [ "${sibs%% *}" = "0" ]; then
        pool_note="repo-wide in_progress runs: NONE while child never started for $((now - watch_started))s — pool appears IDLE (gh-172 zombie signature possible; cannot be confirmed — the runners API is 403 for this token)"
        echo "::warning::$pool_note — NO cancel (gh-1903); if this is a real zombie the leg timeout surfaces the full diagnostic"
      else
        pool_note="repo-wide $sibs"
        echo "sibling activity — $sibs — the queued child is waiting behind these; healthy, no cancel, no stall timer (gh-1903)"
      fi
    else
      pool_note="pool liveness probe FAILED (gh/API unreachable) — pool idleness can be neither established nor excluded"
      echo "pool liveness probe failed — cannot observe, cannot judge (gh-172); no cancel regardless (gh-1903)"
    fi
  fi
  sleep "$poll"
done

conclusion="${status#*/}"
echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
exit 1

Risk: an orphaned never-started child may publish unattended when the pool revives (gh-1903 containment withheld, not waived)" >&2

# Fixed: the probe now counts `queued` runs before idleness is ever claimed

Took option (a) — and went slightly further in the same spirit. The probe is now a **single unfiltered repo-wide listing** (`gh run list --limit 100 --json databaseId,displayTitle,status`, no `--status` filter) that filters out completed runs and our own child, then buckets the rest by status:

- `0 queued, 0 in_progress` → the **only** shape that logs `pool appears IDLE (gh-172 zombie signature possible)` — the header comment's claim is now true.
- `>0 queued, 0 in_progress` → new `queued sibling activity` line: the child is queued behind runs the old probe was blind to — no idle claim, no wolf-cry (this is the exact 2026-10-26 healthy-window shape).
- `>0 in_progress` → the existing `sibling activity` line, now with per-run statuses in the detail.

This also fixes both distortions that rode along:

- **Truncation**: `--limit 20` → `--limit 100`, and because the jq filters by `.status != "completed"` rather than asking the API for one status, a saturated pool can no longer read "0" through a truncated page.
- **Unfiltered** beats two per-status calls: one listing, one API call per probe interval, statuses bucketed client-side.

The header comment (formerly line 33) and the in-loop comment block are rewritten to the new invariant: *only a repo-wide list empty in BOTH `queued` and `in_progress` while the child never started suggests pool idleness — and even then the script does not cancel.*

**Tests (TDD — RED first, all failed against the old script):**

- New `(b2)` test: queued sibling with nothing `in_progress` → no `pool appears IDLE` warning, `queued sibling activity` logged, still no cancel, leg green.
- New fixture shape: `siblings.json` entries now carry `status`; the stub distinguishes the probe from the correlation listing by the absence of `--workflow` (the probe is unfiltered now) instead of the presence of `--status`.
- Test `(e)` updated: the read-only-probe assertion now matches the unfiltered `run list --limit 100` invocation.

`dart test test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28/28 green.

# Fixed: the trap now re-observes once and cancels only what fresh state proves never-started

Implemented the fresh re-check (the reviewer's primary suggestion), with the cancel **withheld** — not merely re-labeled — when the fresh observation fails. The trap now:

1. **Fresh re-observation**: one `gh run view "$run_id" --json status,conclusion,jobs` with the same atomic poll jq (status/conclusion/running-count in one call). The trap is not latency-sensitive — the leg is already dead and this is one API call.
2. **Cancel only when fresh proves never-started** — status `queued`/`in_progress` with **zero** running jobs. The diagnostic prints the fresh observation (`NEVER STARTED (fresh re-observation: queued/- 0; …)`), so `NEVER STARTED` is now a statement about live state, not a stale cache.
3. **Child started between the last poll and the TERM** (fresh running-jobs > 0) → **no cancel**; the diagnostic names exactly that: `STARTED between the last poll and this TERM (fresh re-observation: …)` — a started child is left to its own per-job server-side timeouts (#344).
4. **Already completed** → `nothing to cancel` with the fresh conclusion.
5. **Fresh check itself fails (API outage)** → **no cancel**: `NOT cancelled: the fresh re-observation FAILED … cannot observe, cannot judge (gh-172)`. This closes the last place the script judged from a cache — every surviving decision is now made on a live observation, honoring *cannot observe ⇒ cannot judge* in the one path that still violated it. The trade-off (an orphaned queued child may publish unattended when the pool revives) is spelled out in the diagnostic: containment is *withheld, not waived* — and in a real outage the `gh run cancel` call would fail anyway.

**Tests (TDD — RED first):**

- New `(c2)` test: TERM after the pool picks the child up between the final poll and the signal → fresh check sees a running job → no cancel, diagnostic names the race. (Deterministic: 1s poll + bash's trap-after-sleep semantics guarantee the second poll never runs, so only the trap can observe the `1` jobs line.)
- New `(c3)` test: TERM during a sustained outage (`view-fail-next` covers polls *and* the fresh check) → no cancel call at all, diagnostic says `NOT cancelled` / `cannot observe`.
- Existing `(c)`/`INT` tests still pin the happy containment path: exactly one targeted cancel of a fresh-observation-proven never-started child.

`dart test test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28/28 green.

# Fixed: `is_jobs` computed once at the top of the stub's `view)` handler

Hoisted. The `--json … jobs` scan now runs once at the top of the `view)` handler into `is_jobs`, and both former copies reuse it:

- the `jobs_body` construction (`if [ "$is_jobs" = "1" ]` around the portable count loop), and
- the output-format / `jobs-served-<id>.log` bookkeeping at the end of the handler.

Behavior is byte-identical (both copies scanned the same args and could never disagree — pure deduplication, as suggested). All 28 tests in `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` stay green, including the served-jobs ground-truth assertions that exercise both reuse sites.

# Rework — PR #1907: review-thread fixes for gh-1903

All 3 open review threads addressed with TDD (failing tests first, then the fix), pushed as `55a58bf495` on `ai/gh-1903`.

## Issues/Notes

- **CI**: no owned violations — `ci_failures.md` reports all checks green; nothing to fix or dispute. No merge conflicts.
- **Review decision**: `NONE` (no concluded review); the 3 open threads were the blocking feedback.
- Also fixed the reviewer's non-thread suggestion #3 from the general review comment (`watch_started=0` made the trap print ~1.7-billion-second elapsed if TERM landed during dispatch/appear): `watch_started` is now taken once at script start, so every elapsed diagnostic is leg-elapsed in every path.
- Shellcheck: the only findings on the touched script are the same info-level `SC2317` (trap-body reachability) and `SC2016` (jq quoting) findings that exist verbatim on the pre-rework script — no new issues.

## Approach

1. **Thread 1 (IMPORTANT — probe blind to `queued`)** — took option (a), generalized: the probe is now a single unfiltered repo-wide `gh run list --limit 100` (completed runs filtered in jq), bucketed by status. The `pool appears IDLE` warning fires only when **both** `queued` and `in_progress` counts are zero; a queued-only pool logs a new `queued sibling activity` line (the exact healthy-window shape from the 2026-10-26 incident). This also fixes the `--limit 20` truncation (`.status != "completed"` filtering means a saturated pool can't read "0" through a truncated page). Header comment rewritten — the "positively establishes pool idleness" claim is now true.
2. **Thread 2 (IMPORTANT — orphan-cancel from stale state)** — the trap now performs one fresh `gh run view` re-observation before deciding: cancel only when fresh state proves never-started (0 running jobs); a child that started between the last poll and the TERM is left alone with a diagnostic naming the race; when the fresh check itself fails (API outage) the cancel is **withheld** with a `cannot observe, cannot judge` diagnostic — closing the last cache-based judgment. The gh-1903 invariant now holds in the one path that still violated it.
3. **Thread 3 (SUGGESTION — duplicated `is_jobs`)** — hoisted: computed once at the top of the stub's `view)` handler and reused in both places.

## Files Modified

- `scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh` — unfiltered status-bucketed liveness probe (queued + in_progress); fresh re-observation in the orphan-cleanup trap with cancel withheld on unobservable state; `watch_started` initialized at script start; header/in-loop comments rewritten to the new invariants.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — stub probe detection switched from `--status` presence to `--workflow` absence (probe is unfiltered now); `is_jobs` hoisted; `siblingRuns` fixtures carry `status`; test `(e)` updated to the new probe invocation.

## Test Coverage

- 3 new tests (all confirmed RED against the old script before the fix):
  - `(b2)` queued sibling with nothing `in_progress` → no idle warning, `queued sibling activity` logged, no cancel, leg green.
  - `(c2)` TERM after a pickup between the last poll and the signal → fresh check proves STARTED → no cancel (deterministic via 1s-poll trap-after-sleep semantics).
  - `(c3)` TERM during a sustained outage → fresh check fails → no cancel call issued, diagnostic says `NOT cancelled` / `cannot observe`.
- Existing AC tests `(a)`–`(e)` and the trap tests `(c)`/`INT` unchanged and still green (fresh-proven never-started child → exactly one targeted cancel).
- `dart test test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` → **28/28 pass** (was 25).
- Adjacent suites touching the same workflows/scripts: `store_automation_guard_test.dart` + `ci_1659_office_addin_matrix_test.dart` → 45/45 pass (73/73 combined, 3 consecutive runs).
- Full unit suite (`dart test --exclude-tags llm,integration`) — see the run linked in the rework log; validation CI on the PR is the final gate.

**Three open review threads, all fixed in code with TDD (RED → GREEN), pushed as `55a58bf495` on `ai/gh-1903`:**

The last cache-based judgment in the script is gone.

3. **Duplicated `is_jobs`** (SUGGESTION): hoisted to a single computation at the top of the stub's `view)` handler.
